item.content:encoded:
This is the second tale I've read (first being Crunch), and I must say it captivated me. The dialogues are natural and realistic, something that the modern writers can't seem to pull off often. Able is scary as balls during every second of his screentime; Bullfrog is a relatable chap with unspoken rants about the misfortunes in his days but dives in head-first anyway; Kitty doesn't speak much, but I adore this character for her actions; and though Fartboy didn't strike me as impressive character-wise, the last part did it for me. Though the idea of simple superpowered human beings is rather underwhelming in the face of a world filled with artifacts and entities of vast anomalous properties.

The weakness of this tale though, is the fact that Project Able's disavowal and Able's defection had very minor consequences. A 500 years old chap and military personnel were sliced and diced, a buliding was blown up, and… that's it. Bullfrog's team was wayyyyyy too effective at neutralizing Able (or am I overestimating his abilities?). It was all very underwhelming compared to Area-25's annihilation in the main article.

Not to mention Able's deployment was for a mission that didn't seem to suit him at all (or should I say excessive force?). A demigod who should be wrestling with mammoths was sent in to chop up tofus and kids, something that was described as so minor that perhaps the assessment team didn't have to do anything at all. Is this just a fodder mission to keep Able from being bored?

The points I mention above are, however, major elements that are impossible to be editted, but Im just pointing it out. It may explain why some readers find this uncaptivating. For me though, this certain qualifies for a +1.

item.content:encoded:
Holy shit this is fucking awesome. The characterization, the setting, the action. Hot damn.

A few nitpicks…

It's too predictable that Able gets loose. I'm not even bothering to spoil that, because it was that predictable. That said, the portrayal of him here - the visuals in particular - was compelling.

The talky scenes do go on a bit too long.

And a style nitpick, because it popped out at me:

"Really. Well, ain't that just fucking great," General Bowe muttered sarcastically. "Well? Tell them the news."

We can tell he was being sarcastic. You don't need to tell us that with a magical adverb.

There are probably other nitpicks like this to be found elsewhere in the text, but I didn't see them, because I was too busy being entertained. And for the record, I really thought - SPOILER

+ show block
– hide block

- that Kitty was going to die.

item.content:encoded:
Enthusiastic agreement, Eskobar.

New standards and changing tastes are all well and good, but old-school has served the site well. The oft-reviled "staff shenaningans" provide most of the themes and ideas that underpin the consensus head-canon. We only do ourselves a disservice in the long run by saying that the old ways are now unacceptable. Guidelines are only useful until one has the experience to break the rules constructively.

This tale is entertaing and I want to know what happens next, that is all that really matters in the end.

Regretfully downvoted. It all seems like a bunch of "We are macho, here are our swear words and jargon also we shoot things" to me. The characters didn't stand out to me, I didn't find myself caring all that much about what was going on, and I ended up drifting or trying to scroll faster while reading it.

e: I've tried reading this three times to see if I just missed what everyone else is praising, but I'm not seeing it. It's still just a bunch of jargon between some barely distinguishable soldiers to me. The action's good, but…I don't know if it's the style or the content or what.
